name: Sheet Pan Tandoori Chicken and Cauliflower

intro_html: Tandoori chicken is one of those dinners that tastes like somebody fussed over it, and it never did. The spice blend does all the work. You whisk it into coconut milk with a little salt and lemon, coat the chicken and a pile of cauliflower, and let one hot oven turn it into dinner. No frying, no babysitting, just a sheet pan and a timer. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is a warm, spiced, weeknight-easy dinner that portions straight into your containers for the week.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5 1/4 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs (2381 g)
Cauliflower (generic (USDA)): 3 1/2 small heads (2 lb or less each), cut into florets (1890 g)
Coconut Milk (Thai Kitchen): 3 1/2 cups full-fat coconut milk (about two 13.5 oz cans plus a third) (840 g)
Red Onion: 3 1/2 small red onions, cut into thin wedges (245 g)
Tandoori Masala (Shan (USDA branded)): 7 tbsp tandoori spice mix (no salt added) (56 g)
Olive Oil: 3 1/2 tbsp olive oil, for the pans (47 g)
Salt (Morton): 3 1/2 tbsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or 5 1/4 tsp fine salt) (32 g)
Fresh Cilantro: 3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp minced fresh cilantro (14 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 5 1/4 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs: ~$16.90. Buy 6 lbs: $19.32.
Cauliflower, 3 1/2 small heads (2 lb or less each), cut into florets: ~$12.76. Buy 4 heads: $15.88.
Coconut Milk, 3 1/2 cups full-fat coconut milk (about two 13.5 oz cans plus a third): ~$3.86. Buy 3 13.5oz cans: $5.51.

Fresh Cilantro, 3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp minced fresh cilantro: ~$0.44. Buy 1 bunch: $1.78.
Pantry seasonings (tandoori masala, salt): ~$3.28. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $38.60 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.76 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $47.75 across 14 servings, roughly $3.41 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $10.07 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $57.82. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a spiced, roasted sheet pan dinner that eats like takeout and preps in one pass. The chicken does the heavy lifting; the cauliflower and one jar of spice stretch it into 14 real dinners.
shop_smart: Chicken thighs are the anchor, so buy the boneless skinless. You want about five and a quarter pounds, which is a couple of the big family packs from the meat case. Thighs stay juicy through a hot roast in a way breasts do not, and they take the tandoori marinade beautifully.

Buy whole heads of cauliflower and cut them down yourself. Three or four small heads, two pounds or less each, cut into florets at home. Whole heads give the marinade the most surface to cling to, and cutting your own florets is a two-minute job with a knife.

Tandoori masala is the whole identity of this dish. Look in the international aisle for a jar of tandoori spice blend, the no-salt-added kind if the shelf has it, since we salt the marinade ourselves. It is the one ingredient you cannot swap out and still call this tandoori.

Full-fat coconut milk carries the marinade. The batch uses three and a half cups, so pick up three of the standard 13.5 ounce cans and you will have it covered with a little left over. Full-fat is the one you want here for body; the light cans thin the marinade out.

Salt, lemon juice, and olive oil are pantry backbone. A few tablespoons of each is all the batch asks, so a single bottle or box of each does this dinner and plenty more. Store brand does the same job as the name on the label.
make_it: Weigh your empty containers (or the storage dish you will pack into) and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which beats eyeballing every container.
Heat the oven to 450 degrees, or 425 convection, with a rack in the middle. Cut the cauliflower into florets and the red onions into thin wedges.
Whisk the coconut milk, tandoori masala, salt, and lemon juice together in a large measuring cup or bowl until it is an even, rusty-orange marinade.
Brush your sheet pans with the olive oil. This is a big batch, so plan on two or three rimmed pans; crowding one pan steams the food instead of roasting it.
Put the cauliflower and onions in a large bowl, pour in about half the marinade, and toss to coat. Shake off the excess and spread them out on the oiled pans.
Add the chicken thighs to the same bowl, pour in the rest of the marinade, and toss to coat. Lay the thighs in a single layer on the pans alongside the vegetables.

Roast 25 to 35 minutes, flipping the cauliflower and rotating the pans about halfway through, until the cauliflower is tender and browned and the chicken reads 165 degrees at the thickest part of a thigh.
Sprinkle the minced cilantro over everything, then weigh and portion as below.
portion_html: Set your container on the scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total across all the pans. Divide that number by 14 and pack that exact weight into each container, giving each one some chicken and some cauliflower. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Heat the oven to 450 degrees, cut the cauliflower into florets, and cut the red onions into thin wedges.
Whisk the coconut milk, tandoori masala, salt, and lemon juice into an even marinade.
Brush two or three sheet pans with olive oil.
Toss the cauliflower and onions in half the marinade and spread them on the pans.
Toss the chicken thighs in the rest of the marinade and lay them on the pans in a single layer.
Roast 25 to 35 minutes, flipping the cauliflower and rotating the pans halfway, until the chicken reads 165 degrees.
Sprinkle with cilantro, then weigh the total and divide across 14 containers.
